## Behaviours decided by a single layer

| Behaviour | Layer | Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| With access-control allow for its network, the same non-loopback client gets an answer | access control | `acl-allow-answers-non-loopback-client` |
| Without any access-control line, a query from ::1 is allowed, although the manual names only 127.0.0.0/8 | access control | `acl-default-allows-ipv6-loopback` |
| Without any access-control line, a query from a non-loopback address is answered with REFUSED, even for local-data | access control | `acl-default-refuses-non-loopback-client` |
| With access-control deny, the client gets no reply at all | access control | `acl-deny-drops-query-without-reply` |
| access-control uses the most specific netblock for the source address, whatever the order of the lines: a /32 refuse beats a /8 written before it and a /24 written after it | access control | `acl-longest-match-wins-regardless-of-order` |
| Under refuse_non_local a name that no local zone covers is refused before it reaches the cache or the iterator | access control after local zones | `acl-refuse-non-local-refuses-other-names` |
| A client under refuse_non_local also gets answers from an auth-zone with for-downstream: yes | access control after local zones | `acl-refuse-non-local-still-answers-auth-zone` |
| A client under refuse_non_local still gets local-data: the local-zone answer comes before the non_local check | access control after local zones | `acl-refuse-non-local-still-answers-local-data` |
| With for-downstream: yes, a CNAME whose target is in the same auth-zone is answered together with the target's data | in-zone CNAME chain in the auth answer | `auth-zone-downstream-cname-in-zone-target-added` |
| With the default cache-max-negative-ttl, an NXDOMAIN whose SOA has TTL and MINIMUM 86400 is cut to 3600 | TTL clamping on reply parse | `cache-max-negative-ttl-default-caps-soa-ttl` |
| Setting cache-max-negative-ttl to 1000 cuts the SOA TTL of an NXDOMAIN (TTL and MINIMUM 86400) to 1000 | TTL clamping on reply parse | `cache-max-negative-ttl-setting-caps-soa-ttl` |
| cache-min-ttl raises the TTL of an upstream answer, and the client already sees the raised TTL on the first reply | TTL clamping on reply parse | `cache-min-ttl-raises-upstream-ttl` |
| The DNS-over-TLS forwarding recipe (tls-cert-bundle, forward-tls-upstream and addr@853#name) passes unbound-checkconf | checkconf coverage | `checkconf-accepts-forward-dot-recipe` |
